voor.When the young men of Gettysburg left: You'd stand on the platform with your family, waving your handkerchief as the train pulled away.
voor.A town of only 2,400 people: On a Sunday morning, you'd hear bells ringing from every direction, one after another.
voor.The most famous young woman: You've probably heard her name, but you may not know her real one.
voor.For the Black families of Gettysburg: If you'd lived in their homes, you'd have listened to every rumour with great care.
voor.The most famous general in the South: You'd have known him at once, sitting straight and calm on his grey horse.
voor.One of the horses the soldiers took: You can imagine how you'd feel, watching your own horse led away.
voor.A quiet cavalry general: You'd see him riding slowly along the ridges, looking carefully at everything.
voor.The Union general was woken: You can picture him, sitting up in bed, still half asleep.
voor.Neither General Lee nor: You might think a great battle is always planned. This one wasn't.
voor.Tillie was sent to a farm: You'd see her climbing into a wagon with a small bundle on her lap.
voor.A young engineer climbed: Stand beside him on the rocks, and you'll see the whole valley below you.
voor.The professor from Maine: You'll remember him, the man who knew Latin, Greek and Hebrew.
voor.On the second night, the Union generals: You'd see their shadows on the walls of that tiny room, in the candlelight.
voor.Jennie Wade was baking: You'd smell the bread rising in that small, warm kitchen.
voor.Just before the great cannonade: You'd hear the clink of their tin plates in the quiet midday heat.
voor.The cannonade at Gettysburg: If you'd been miles away, you'd have looked up at a clear sky and wondered about the thunder.
voor.After the charge, General Lee: You'd hear his voice, quiet and steady, as the men came back.
voor.When Lee's army left: You'd see the wagons going by for hours and hours in the rain.
voor.When Tillie finally came home: You'd see her walking slowly up Baltimore Street, tired and dusty.
voor.A great tent hospital: You'd see the white tents from far off, like a field of sails.

voor.In the new cemetery, every grave: You'd walk along the rows and see that no stone stood taller than another.
voor.The main speaker at Gettysburg: You'd need to be patient if you came to hear him.
voor.President Lincoln was only invited: You might think the President would be the main speaker. He wasn't.
voor.When a crowd asked Lincoln: You'd hear the crowd laughing under the window.
voor.The night before his speech: You can picture him reading it twice, by the lamp.
